Subject/topic/subtopic/lesson, this file structure is in alphanumeric order, 
meaning that when the file structure is scanned through, all lessons are returned 
in order. Hence the file name structure, “<topic number>_<subtopic 
number>_<lesson number>_<lesson name>”. Within each lesson will be a 
lesson.json, this file defines the lesson’s name and lesson order, i.e. the first 
three activities will be questions of a certain type and the last two will be videos. 
Additionally, within this folder are two more folders: one for the video.mp4s and 
another for question.jsons. Each question type will have a different JSON format. 
The decision to use DynamoDB over the alternative Relational Database Service 
(RDS), was primarily driven by cost-effectiveness, simplicity, and superior 
scalability. DynamoDB, offers a fully managed NoSQL database system, with 
abstracted scalability, removing the added operational complexity linked with 
relational database systems (AWS, 2024). Horizontal scalability is critical to this 
project’s implementation, which demands high availability and fast data access, 
with potentially rapidly fluctuating loads, based around school times and day and 
night cycles. Additionally, the pay-per-request pricing structure for DynamoDB, 
offers to reduce costs further, removing the need to invest in hardware and 
potentially over provision. 
Cognito is a critical element of the project’s infrastructure, for managing user 
identities and the user’s leader board data. This strategy enhances security and 
simplifies user state management, while unifying relevant data into a single 
place. Additionally, the flexibility of Cognito permits fast and efficient integration 
with other services.
